1st minute kick-off from Lelean kick was a short scrum to Grammar, and a penalty was awarded in the first minute.

3rd minute: Grammar scores the first try with a rumbling maul to Captain Waisale Bolakoro, Grammar leads Lelean 5-0.

5th minute: Lelean attacking the Grammar line maintaining possesion while Grammar maintains good defence.

7th minute Grammar wins another scrum and awarded a penalty.

10th minute Grammar awarded their third penalty in the scrum and kbnows Lelean scrum is weak.

12th minute Grammar given another penalty as they opt for a line out in Lelleans 22 metre line.

14th minute Grammar scores there second try to extend their lead through hooker to extend their lead 12-0.

18th minute Lelean drops the ball while attacking and giving Grammar possesion again.

19th minute Grammar attacking the Lelean line again, showing their class and dominance.

22nd minute Lelean was awarded a scrum, and Grammar pressured them and won the ball back.

25th minute Grammar hooker scores his second try to extend their lead 19-0.

27th minute Lelean score there first try to reduce the deficit through a charge down SGS leads 19-7.

33th minute second penatly to Grammar kick misses Grammar leads 19-7.

Second half kicks off Lelean attacks the Grammar line and awarded a penalty try as they close the deficit 19-14.

38th minute Grammar hooker scores a hattrick to extend their 24- 14.

41st minute Grammar awarded a penalty and LMS given a yellow card Grammar with numerical advantage.

47th minute Grammar scores another try to their flanker to extend their lead 29-14.

50th minute Grammar given another penalty and they can not go pass the SGS line.

53rd minute Lelean is given their second yellow card

56th minute SGS fly half scores another try to extend their lead 36-14.

59th minute Grammar continues to dominte possesion and attacks the LMS line.

66th minute Grammar wins offside penalty.

70th minute Lelean awarded secondf penalty try to go down to SGS 36-21.

item.title: Minister condemns video mocking sign language
item.description: Sign language is not a joke, a costume or a prop for entertainment. It is an essential means of communication and an important expression of language, culture and identity for the Deaf community. item.content:encoded:
Sign language is not a joke, a costume or a prop for entertainment. It is an essential means of communication and an important expression of language, culture and identity for the Deaf community.

This is the comment from the Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection, Sashi Kiran, who has strongly condemned an insensitive video recently posted by students of a local tertiary institution, which appears to mock sign language and members of the Deaf community.

Kiran says making fun of sign language is deeply disrespectful and reinforces harmful attitudes and stereotypes that persons with disabilities continue to face.

The Minister says every person, regardless of ability, has the right to be treated with dignity, equality and respect.

She says incidents of this nature undermine the collective efforts of Government, organisations of persons with disabilities, civil society, educational institutions and communities to remove barriers and create a more inclusive Fiji.

Kiran stresses that inclusion goes beyond policies and programmes, and requires people to examine their attitudes, challenge discrimination and ensure that persons with disabilities are respected, represented and valued in every aspect of society.

The Ministry urges the students involved and the institution concerned to reflect on the harm caused and use this incident as an opportunity for learning, accountability and positive change.
